chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man came to a man.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was married (muhsan), then upon him is the killing (qatl), and if he was not married, then upon him is the whipping (jald). I said: 'So what is upon the passive one (al-muta')?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the killing in every state, whether he was married or not married.'

key_terms.مُحْصَنٌ: A married man (or one with a free, chaste wife)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in penalty for the active and passive partners in sodomy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinct hadd penalties for sodomy, emphasizing the severity of the act by prescribing death for the passive partner regardless of marital status, a view often contrasted with the majority opinion that requires marriage for the death penalty. It highlights the juristic distinction between the active partner, whose punishment varies by being 'muhsan' (married) or not, and the passive partner, whose penalty is fixed. This ruling underscores the gravity attributed to the receptive role in Shia legal tradition.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al hassan Bin Ali, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man comes to a man’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he was married, so upon him is the killing, and if does not happen to be married, so upon him is the whipping’. So I said, ‘So what is upon the passive one?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is the killing upon every state, whether he was married, or without marriage’.
